intent: Hold the best-raced geometry unchanged (±0.03 m row, 16 mm footprint, y = 0.04, wheels, body and mass as before) so the Integrator's restored kp 1.2 / kd 0.4 controller is judged on the platform it was tuned for. Expected result: a score near 69.46, with max error about 0.062 m and line loss at about 1.0 to 1.1 events per run. This race confirms that the iteration 4 drop was the gain, not the geometry. I am not expecting a new best score from this race. Next iteration, I plan to race the ±0.04 m row at 16 mm with kp 1.2, which tests the widening on its own. I am not committing to a forward offset, since slalom oscillation (0.145 to 0.147) is below the 0.15 trigger.
learning: Open hypotheses: (1) confirmed-gain hypothesis: a score near 69.46 at kp 1.2 would confirm that iteration 4's drop was the gain change, not the ±0.04 row; (2) if the ±0.04 row at kp 1.2 next iteration gives a higher line-loss-free progress than 0.210 on the s-bend, the wider coverage edge is helping, and the remaining limit is the controller's edge response; (3) if line loss stays at 1.0 or more with the wider row, the 16 mm footprint may be adding edge noise, and the 12 mm test at the same spacing would be the discriminator. Please report, in integration feedback, the progress at the first line-loss event on each track and the max error at that moment, and whether the loss occurs at start-up. That separates coverage-edge loss from controller overshoot, although it is not one of the allowed measurement names.
rationale:
The race evidence is consistent across iterations. The best raced design is the ±0.03 m row at 16 mm with y = 0.04 (iteration 3, 69.46). Iteration 5 reproduced that score exactly, so the simulator is deterministic for this geometry. Every run across all tracks still ends off track at max error about 0.062 m, against the 0.06 m limit. Body width cannot relax that limit within the allowed range, so the limit is the binding failure. Line loss persists at 1.0 to 1.1 events per run.

Iteration 4 widened the row to ±0.04 m and lowered kp from 1.2 to 1.0 in the same race. Progress fell on the s-bend (0.210 to 0.160) and oval (0.184 to 0.170), and line loss did not fall. The Integrator's feedback reads this as most likely a gain effect, not a coverage effect. The Integrator has now restored kp 1.2 and kd 0.4, and built that controller for the ±0.03 m row. They asked that this race hold ±0.03 m, 16 mm, y = 0.04, so the controller is judged on the geometry it was tuned for. I took that advice. Changing the row now would confound the result with the controller restore.

I am not repeating the iteration 5 candidate unchanged. I am holding its geometry, which is the same as iteration 3, because the controller has changed. The purpose of this race is to confirm the controller restore (expected score near 69.46). The next geometry test, as the Integrator asked, is the ±0.04 m row at 16 mm with kp 1.2. That isolates the widening from the gain change, which the iteration 4 race could not do. If the ±0.04 row still leaves line loss at 1.0 or more, a 12 mm footprint at the same spacing is the next test, to check whether 16 mm edge noise is adding s-bend oscillation.
